title: Canonical event serialization is ambiguous for delimiter-bearing fields
evidence: serialize_canonical concatenates event_id, comma-joined parents, tick, payload and signature using unescaped delimiters.
trigger: Two otherwise identical events with payload/signature pairs (a|b,c) and (a,b|c).
impact: Both serialize to the same canonical bytes and graph digest despite different event content; the reference cannot serve as an integrity oracle.

title: Exported global hash does not bind artifact state
evidence: global_hash is SHA256 of the constant bytes artifact_state_v3; program and canonical_graph are not included.
trigger: Export different programs or ledger states through B60MinimalVM.export_artifact.
impact: Every manifest has the same global_hash, preventing consumers of this example field from detecting artifact substitution.

title: Reference CLI announces proof dispatch that never occurs
evidence: static_proof at lines 114-116 is pass; export_artifact returns only in-memory values, while CLI prints Proof IR extracted. Dispatched to Lean/Coq Backends.
trigger: Run any non-HALTED reference program.
impact: Example output misrepresents absent formal verification as completed proof generation and dispatch. No production proof bypass is alleged.

title: Real Ollama examples return the Tier 1 canned response
evidence: call_tier1 ignores req and returns a fixed success after 100ms; with_tier3 uses a 2000ms T1 timeout. poc_t3_ollama_real.rs:40,59 and poc_oracle_nexus.rs:41,45 use that constructor.
trigger: Run either linked real-inference example with default gateway configuration.
impact: The request never reaches Ollama and a placeholder is presented as resolved inference; the attestor wraps it as ExogenousInjection.

title: Configurable policy can enable Tier 3 for Ring 0
evidence: RingPolicy.t3_allowed only tests vector membership (127-128); with_config accepts any vector; dispatch does not separately exclude target_ring==0 despite INV_CB_01.
trigger: Construct with_config with t3_allowed_rings=[0], a Tier 3 engine, and a T1 timeout shorter than its mock latency.
impact: A Ring 0 request enters the Tier 2/Tier 3 race contrary to the documented unconditional fail-stop invariant. This is a gateway routing invariant violation, not evidence of protected-effect execution.

title: Gemini generation tool returns a canned response without invoking Gemini
evidence: The registered gemini_labs_generate tool formats a fixed response_text; GEMINI_API_KEY is read but no API client/request appears anywhere in this module. Result and telemetry label it GEMINI_GENERATE (149-152).
trigger: Invoke gemini_labs_generate with FastMCP installed.
impact: Callers receive a purported generated response independent of prompt content, and the ledger records a model generation that never occurred.

title: Receipt producer labels a public hash prefix as an Ed25519 signature
evidence: signature_ed25519 is the literal prefix sig_ed25519_ plus merkle_root[:32]; no private key/sign operation exists. Both MCP tools return this object (147-152,161-165), and append_auto_log persists it.
trigger: Generate a receipt through either MCP tool.
impact: Returned and persisted receipts cannot provide the advertised signature authentication; anyone can construct that field. No downstream authorization bypass is claimed.

title: Arithmetic overflow escapes VM fail-closed handling
evidence: mul_scalar multiplies accumulated u128 units without checked_mul and casts seconds to u64; add at line 35 also uses unchecked u64 addition. execute directly calls both. ffi.rs:143-163 exposes execution through extern C without panic handling.
trigger: Repeated SexaMulRational or SexaAdd instructions exceed the seconds range; registers are also public to Rust callers.
impact: Release arithmetic can wrap or truncate and return success with an incorrect result; checked builds panic rather than poisoning the manifest, and panic crossing the C ABI can abort the host process.

title: Out-of-range jumps return successful execution
evidence: Jump assigns the decoded u16 directly to pc; the execute loop only checks pc < bytecode.len() and returns Ok after it ends. Conditional jump branches do the same. ffi.rs:154-160 converts Ok to return code 0.
trigger: Bytecode containing a jump target beyond the supplied buffer.
impact: Malformed control flow is accepted as successful completion with a running manifest, rather than rejected.

title: Snapshot engine resolves its root above the repository
evidence: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parents[2]; for repo/scripts/c5_l1_ledger/ledger_snapshot_engine.py this is the repository parent. DB_PATH and SNAPSHOT_DIR derive from it at 25-26.
trigger: Run the script from its checked-in location without monkeypatching globals.
impact: It reads or creates the parent directory cortex.db and writes snapshots outside this repository, rather than backing up this repository cortex.db; the missing-source branch can silently produce an empty snapshot. Existing tests patch both paths and therefore conceal this error.

title: Second-resolution filenames cause snapshot collisions
evidence: Timestamp uses %Y%m%d_%H%M%S for both destination database (46) and manifest (70), without a unique suffix or retry. VACUUM INTO targets this same file at 52.
trigger: Two calls create_snapshot occur within the same UTC second with an existing source database.
impact: The second VACUUM INTO fails on the existing nonempty target, disrupting a valid backup request; concurrent writers may also contend for the manifest name.

title: Parallel face-swap jobs share one identity embedding file
evidence: TEMP_EMBEDDINGS_PATH is the fixed /tmp/c5_source_embeddings.npz at line 96; every parent overwrites it at 627 and workers load that same path at 812, without a session path argument or lock.
trigger: Start a second pipeline with different identities after the first writes embeddings but before all first-job workers have loaded them.
impact: Workers can use the other job's identities, mix identities across chunks, or fail while reading a concurrently rewritten NPZ.

title: Worker suppresses encoder failure and can deliver truncated video
evidence: The frame write catches BrokenPipeError/IOError and breaks at 428-432; ffmpeg_proc.wait() at 442 has its return code discarded. The worker returns normally; parent only checks Python child return codes at 700-704 before concatenation.
trigger: FFmpeg exits after writing a partial but parseable chunk, or input decoding stops early.
impact: A worker exits successfully despite missing frames; concat/mux can accept a shorter valid MP4 and pipeline prints DONE without a frame-count check.

title: Bind finding metadata into receipt verification
evidence: generate_receipt root at 96 uses only payload_hash and hardware hash; verify_receipt at 116-118 recomputes those same two leaves. claim_id/advisory_id/domain/finding_summary/risk_score/timestamp are excluded. compute_claim_hash includes them but its output is never compared by verify_receipt. Pipeline orchestrator imports/creates this attester at 24/86.
trigger: A receipt is copied with a different advisory, summary, risk score or timestamp while keeping its payload hash, hardware anchor and root.
impact: verify_receipt still returns true for altered claim metadata, despite documenting receipt hash coherence.

title: Identity forging truncates existing master seed and is not atomic
evidence: touch(exist_ok=True) followed by open(...,"w") replaces master_seed.enc unconditionally; no existing-identity rejection, temporary-file rename, or fsync. Cross-file consumer seal_bounty_aeon.py:126-129 calls forge_identity after any load exception.
trigger: A caller attempts recovery from a wrong passphrase/decryption error, or process interruption occurs during replacement.
impact: The existing identity can be silently replaced or left unreadable, losing the signing identity needed to verify historical records.

title: Genomic mechanics metadata is shifted onto the next primitive
evidence: ONC-145 describes TMB as somatic mutations per megabase, but carries chromosomal imbalance/spindle metadata (1791–1795). Its TMB formula and threshold instead appear under ONC-146 Mutational signatures (1809–1813); COSMIC signature metadata is under ONC-147 APOBEC, and the shift continues through ONC-154 TERT carrying the preceding ecDNA circular-amplicon mechanics.
trigger: Read get("ONC-146")["genomic_mechanics"] or otherwise export the structured PRIMITIVES records.
impact: Structured records return mechanics associated with a different named primitive, contradicting neighboring descriptions. No production clinical use or medical outcome established; this is a corpus association defect.

title: Terminal generation failure is swallowed and retried until timeout
evidence: pollStatus throws on status FAILED at 148-149 inside the try, but its catch at 152-157 logs every non-AbortError and continues the polling loop.
trigger: generation.getTaskStatus returns a terminal FAILED status.
impact: The extension continues issuing requests for the remaining polling window and eventually reports a generic timeout instead of the actual server failure.

title: Verified commit is independent of the causally bound descriptor
evidence: verified_commit creates a temporary file and persists to caller-supplied target_path (70-73); neither self.fd nor self.inode nor the original path is consulted.
trigger: Bind an authorized file, then invoke verified_commit with another target path, or replace a destination parent after binding.
impact: PoC writes a destination that was never checked by bind_causal_path; its demonstrated binding does not constrain the commit.

title: Lean example ignores sequence continuity when declaring causality preserved
evidence: validateTransition names current sequence _currentSeq and checks parity only; chunks start validation from 0,false independently.
trigger: Validate an odd WriteBegin followed by any even WriteEnd, including a decreasing sequence; or compare independently validated chunks.
impact: The proof accepts nonmonotonic sequences and provides no cross-chunk continuity, while line 48 declares end-to-end causality preservation.

title: Legal oracle turns network failures into healthy empty result
evidence: Fetch exception returns([],[]); main writes sitrep, prints no threats and operational verdict.
trigger: Fetch fails or times out.
impact: Unavailable scan becomes indistinguishable from successful zero-result scan.

title: Stress gate never asserts validation and rejection counts
evidence: The loop counts successful valid calls and rejected invalid calls, but final exit status checks only average latency and memory delta. Invalid calls that return normally are silently accepted.
trigger: A regression makes validate_mcp_contract return True for every input or False for valid inputs without raising.
impact: The stress script can exit 0 and announce success while contract rejection or valid-input acceptance is broken. No physical conclusion follows from these measurements.

title: Do not issue a complete forensic attestation when captures are absent
evidence: Missing primary captures are silently skipped (115); missing session captures only warn (143-144). The generated Claim/Base/Confidence/Catalog_Attestation at 157-162 always declares all 11 verified.
trigger: Evidence directory exists but one or more mapped captures are missing.
impact: The generated catalog asserts a complete verified evidence set while containing fewer entries; hashes identify read bytes but the script does not validate the asserted chronology or provenance.

title: Unboxing claims Touch ID readiness from file existence
evidence: check_touchid_gate returns swift_gate.exists() and platform.system()==Darwin; line 71 renders this as Secure Enclave TouchID [LISTO].
trigger: Run on a Darwin host with the helper file but unavailable or unprovisioned Touch ID.
impact: The onboarding output declares a security prerequisite ready without checking hardware, provisioning, or executing an attestation.

title: Causal verifier still targets removed packages directory
evidence: packages_dir is repo_root/packages at line 18; bft_dir derives from it at line 29 and absent-directory check immediately returns False at lines 30–32. Read-only metadata shows no packages directory; assigned real BFT sources reside in 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60/bft.
trigger: Run this verifier on the current checkout.
impact: The verification exits before examining current BFT sources or WAL; its structural check also requires the obsolete packages/babylon60 path.

title: Telemetry monitor displays fabricated security evidence as live state
evidence: main creates SharedManifest::new locally at line 112; render_screen prints fixed SUPPORTED NEMESIS claims, SEALED attestation (96-100), fixed receipt records (84-87), and ACTIVE hardware gate (35). No receipt or gate evidence is read.
trigger: Run babylon_top, including on a host with no running kernel or attestation evidence.
impact: Operator is shown successful security checks and committed effects that have never been observed.

title: Gateway fallback example calls an undeclared Anthropic provider
evidence: The fenced example imports createAiGateway, createOpenAI and generateText and defines only openai, then invokes anthropic(...) in its fallback array. No Anthropic import or initialization exists in the file.
trigger: Adapt the advertised automatic fallback block using the preceding imports and provider setup.
impact: TypeScript reports an unresolved identifier (or JavaScript throws ReferenceError); the documented fallback example cannot run as shown.

title: Concurrent synthesis invocations share one intermediate WAV
evidence: raw_tmp is the fixed /tmp/f5_raw_synthesis.wav; sf.write precedes a separate ffmpeg invocation reading that path.
trigger: Two synthesis processes overlap between writing the WAV and FFmpeg opening it.
impact: One requested output can contain another speaker or text; intermediate audio is also left behind.

title: Password audit requires plaintext secret in command-line arguments
evidence: Usage instructs passing the password as $1 and assigns PASSWORD="$1"; no hidden terminal or stdin input path exists.
trigger: User follows the documented invocation with a real password.
impact: Password can enter shell history and process argument inspection despite the network k-anonymity protection.

title: YouTube URL and output directory are interpolated into a shell
evidence: run_cmd uses subprocess.run(shell=True) at line 9; URL is placed in double quotes at 17/36/42 and output_dir at 36.
trigger: A supplied URL or output directory contains shell substitution such as $(command), or a quote that terminates the quoted argument.
impact: Executing the acquisition script runs attacker-controlled shell commands with the operator account privileges.
